data.claim: With policy=[pins_regenerate] and pins.regenerate in standing_verbs, PO.apply approves a recipe-only canon for an agent holding one live item; with the rule off or any limit unmet, a person is asked
data.falsifier: operator_gate returns ok via policy with the rule off, for a recipe outside the allowlist, for a second use, outside the window, for another identity, or for a tier-3 or L2 site
data.mechanism: Canon.item holds the recipe name, so apply() must resolve the work item from the agent's lease; the rule predicate reads the primary's recipes file and shared_globs
data.probe: pytest tests/test_approvals_standing_pins.py (before the change 8 of 21 failed: the on-path tests; after, 21 pass; four mutations of the code each fail a test)
data.question: Does a registered standing rule for pins.regenerate answer an agent's bare 'pins regenerate --only R' without a person, only when switched on, only for allowlisted generated recipes, once per recipe and work item?

chunk_findings.detail: `_recipe_untouched` only checks that `recipes_file` is clean in `repo` and that the recipe parsed from `repo` equals the recipe parsed from the current `primary`. It does not detect an edit that has been committed, nor an edit to `primary`. Given the common input where the agent runs the command in the same checkout (`repo == primary`) with `pins_regenerate` enabled, the agent can edit recipe `R`’s `regen` command in `recipes_file`, run `git add recipes_file && git commit`, then invoke `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` as an agent with no `--approval`. `git status --porcelain -- recipes_file` is empty, `mine == trusted` because both loads read the same committed edited file, so `_recipe_untouched` returns `True`; the edited-recipe guard is skipped and the standing rule answers, running the edited recipe without a person.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_recipe_untouched

chunk_findings.detail: The edited-recipe guard is bypassed when the agent supplies a non-empty approval value, including `--approval request`. The condition `not approval` is false for `CN.REQUEST`, so `_recipe_untouched` is never consulted even when the recipe has been edited. Given `pins_regenerate` enabled and recipe `R` edited, an agent can run `ddflow pins regenerate --only R --approval request`; the canonical approval is still `CN.REQUEST`, the request path that standing rules can answer, and the command can be answered without a person despite the edited recipe.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_regenerate_approval

chunk_findings.detail: For a `PINS_VERB` canon, `apply` now resolves `it = _acting_item(state, canon, cfg)` before any enabled standing rule has been found. If `_rule_stamp` then returns `None` because `pins_regenerate` is absent from `cfg.approvals.policy`, because its window is closed, or because `policy_max_uses` has been exhausted, control falls through to the retry approval block. That block only checks `canon.site.min_level <= 1`, `retry_armed(cfg, canon)`, and `person_only_target(it, canon.verb, canon.target)`. Concrete input: `cfg.approvals.policy = []` (rule off), a recipe in the new default allowlist such as `readme-knobs` for which `_acting_item` finds a work item, an L1/non-T3 site, `auto_approve_after_retries` satisfied so `retry_armed(cfg, canon)` is true, and `person_only_target(...)` false. `apply` returns an approval for `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` even though the standing pins rule is off. Previously a pins canon named a recipe, so `state.items.get(canon.item)` was normally `None` and the function returned before the retry path; this change makes the retry path reachable for pins and bypasses the pins-specific enabled/window/use checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: `_rule_stamp` intentionally returns `None` when `canon.site.tier == sites.T3`, and its comment states that a policy answer is “never a tier-3 act.” However, the retry fallback in `apply` does not enforce tier. Given a tier-T3 site with `canon.site.min_level == 1`, `retry_armed(cfg, canon)` true, and `person_only_target(...)` false, `_rule_stamp` returns `None` at the tier check, then `apply` still enters the retry block and returns an approval. This lets a tier-3 act get an automatic answer without a person, violating the new invariant asserted in the same change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The new paragraph says “A use opens or extends the standing window, like any in-scope fire,” but the standing window is described earlier as a global window bounded by `standing_window_s` and `standing_verbs`, not as a per-rule window. With this documented behavior, an agent that gets one auto-approved `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` can open or extend the same standing window that other enabled standing rules consume. For example, if `approvals.policy` includes both `pins_regenerate` and `complete.force`, and `standing_verbs` includes `pins.regenerate` and `complete.force`, the agent’s allowed regenerate fire can extend the global window and then a subsequent `complete.force` can be answered by policy without a person. That widens the scope of other standing rules beyond the explicit `pins_regenerate` approval and can defeat the expired-window bound by letting agent-triggered in-scope uses keep the window alive.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/approvals.md:79

chunk_findings.detail: The third assertion `assert again.exit == 3, again  # one use per recipe and item` does not actually prove the one-use cap. The preceding `off = _door(proj, monkeypatch, local=False)` call is expected to file a pending person ask, and the test never checks that that ask has been resolved or that the third refusal is caused by the policy use cap rather than by the still-pending ask (or another pending gate condition). If `operator_gate` refuses a repeat request while a person ask is pending, this test would pass even if `policy_max_uses` were not enforced, so it fails as a falsifier for the claimed one-use limit.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_approvals_standing_pins.py:test_the_door_refuses_while_off_and_answers_itself_when_switched_on

chunk_findings.detail: The edited-recipe guard does not actually block a standing-rule answer; it only changes the approval mode to `CN.REQUEST`, and it is skipped entirely when the agent supplies `--approval request`. With `pins_regenerate` enabled and a generated/allowlisted recipe whose definition has been edited, running `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` with no approval makes `_recipe_untouched` return false, so the new branch sets `approval = CN.REQUEST`. The subsequent approval-consumption path treats that as the normal standing-rule request path, so the policy can answer the request and the command returns ok without a person. The same bypass is available explicitly via `ddflow pins regenerate --only R --approval request`, because `not approval` is false and `_recipe_untouched` is never evaluated. To enforce “an edited recipe is never answered by a standing rule,” the code must refuse or mark the request person-only, not merely set it to `CN.REQUEST`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_regenerate_approval

chunk_findings.detail: The new `pins_regenerate` standing rule is registered with `_generated_recipe` as its only `when` predicate, but that predicate checks only the recipe allowlist and shared globs; it does not require a live lease/work item. The new `_acting_item` helper and the new optional `work_item` plumbing are not referenced by the rule condition or by any changed call to `used`/`_approved`, so the rule as defined can be satisfied by an agent that is not working an item. For example, with `[approvals].policy_pin_recipes = ["R"]`, a primary-checkout recipe `R` whose `files` are all shared, and an agent with no live lease, `_generated_recipe` returns true. If the standing-rule evaluator then records the approval via `_approved(...)` with the default empty `work_item`, the agent receives a `policy:pins_regenerate` answer without a person and without a live work-item lease, contrary to the stated “answers an agent that is working an item, never an identity that merely names one” constraint. The same empty-work-item recording also makes that use invisible to a later `used(state, "pins_regenerate", "R", work_item="W")` call because the stored ask text lacks the required `\n  work item: W\n  approved by standing rule: pins_regenerate` suffix, so a subsequent use for real work item `W` can bypass the “once per recipe and work item” limit.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py` (`RULES["pins_regenerate"]`, `_generated_recipe`, `_acting_item`, `used`, `_approved`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new pins branch makes `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` reach the generic retry auto-approval path even when the `pins_regenerate` standing rule is not approving. `apply` now sets `it = _acting_item(...)` for `PINS_VERB`, so the old `if it is None: return None` guard no longer sends pins commands to a person; if `_rule_stamp` returns `None`—for example because `pins_regenerate` is not in `cfg.approvals.policy`, the recipe is outside `approvals.policy_pin_recipes`, the per-recipe/work-item use limit is exhausted, or the window is expired—`apply` continues to the retry branch. Given a pins canon whose retry count has reached `cfg.approvals.auto_approve_after_retries`, on an L1 non-T3 site, with no person-only gate matched by `person_only_target(it, canon.verb, canon.target)`, `apply` returns a retry stamp and the agent gets an approval without a person. This also defeats the new tier-3 guard because that check is only inside `_rule_stamp`, while the retry path checks only `min_level <= 1`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The added documentation states that a `pins_regenerate` use “opens or extends the standing window, like any in-scope fire.” Because the standing window is the shared mechanism that suppresses human approval for verbs listed in `standing_verbs`, this documents a way for a non-gate command to widen coverage of other standing rules. For example, if the operator has enabled both `pins_regenerate` and `complete.force` in `approvals.policy`/`standing_verbs`, an agent can run `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` once for a live work item; per this text that opens/extends the standing window, and a later `ddflow complete --force` within `standing_window_s` can then be answered as `policy:complete.force` without a fresh person approval. That is wrong because `pins_regenerate` should not broaden the approval window available to other standing rules.
chunk_findings.title: docs/ddflow/approvals.md:79

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `used` logic does not fail closed for all drifted answer texts. It treats only a text with no line starting with `  work item: ` as an unattributed use; if the drifted text contains such a line with any unexpected remainder, `_work_item_of` returns that remainder and the use is counted only against that exact remainder. Given `policy_max_uses=1` and a policy answer for recipe `R`/item `T1` whose text is `...
  work item: T1 (auto)
  approved by standing rule: pins_regenerate`, `_work_item_of` returns `"T1 (auto)"`, so `used(state, "pins_regenerate", "R", "T1")` returns 0. The next `pins.regenerate` for the same recipe and item sees the cap as unused and can be answered automatically again, bypassing the one-use-per-recipe-per-item rule. The added test only exercises a text with the marker removed entirely.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:used

chunk_findings.detail: The edited-recipe guard does not actually block a standing-rule answer; it only changes the approval mode to `CN.REQUEST`, and it is skipped entirely when the agent supplies `--approval request`. With `pins_regenerate` enabled and a generated/allowlisted recipe whose definition has been edited, running `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` with no approval makes `_recipe_untouched` return false, so the new branch sets `approval = CN.REQUEST`. The subsequent approval-consumption path treats that as the normal standing-rule request path, so the policy can answer the request and the command returns ok without a person. The same bypass is available explicitly via `ddflow pins regenerate --only R --approval request`, because `not approval` is false and `_recipe_untouched` is never evaluated. To enforce “an edited recipe is never answered by a standing rule,” the code must refuse or mark the request person-only, not merely set it to `CN.REQUEST`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_regenerate_approval

chunk_findings.detail: The new `pins_regenerate` standing rule is registered with `_generated_recipe` as its only `when` predicate, but that predicate checks only the recipe allowlist and shared globs; it does not require a live lease/work item. The new `_acting_item` helper and the new optional `work_item` plumbing are not referenced by the rule condition or by any changed call to `used`/`_approved`, so the rule as defined can be satisfied by an agent that is not working an item. For example, with `[approvals].policy_pin_recipes = ["R"]`, a primary-checkout recipe `R` whose `files` are all shared, and an agent with no live lease, `_generated_recipe` returns true. If the standing-rule evaluator then records the approval via `_approved(...)` with the default empty `work_item`, the agent receives a `policy:pins_regenerate` answer without a person and without a live work-item lease, contrary to the stated “answers an agent that is working an item, never an identity that merely names one” constraint. The same empty-work-item recording also makes that use invisible to a later `used(state, "pins_regenerate", "R", work_item="W")` call because the stored ask text lacks the required `\n  work item: W\n  approved by standing rule: pins_regenerate` suffix, so a subsequent use for real work item `W` can bypass the “once per recipe and work item” limit.
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py` (`RULES["pins_regenerate"]`, `_generated_recipe`, `_acting_item`, `used`, `_approved`)

chunk_findings.detail: The new pins branch makes `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` reach the generic retry auto-approval path even when the `pins_regenerate` standing rule is not approving. `apply` now sets `it = _acting_item(...)` for `PINS_VERB`, so the old `if it is None: return None` guard no longer sends pins commands to a person; if `_rule_stamp` returns `None`—for example because `pins_regenerate` is not in `cfg.approvals.policy`, the recipe is outside `approvals.policy_pin_recipes`, the per-recipe/work-item use limit is exhausted, or the window is expired—`apply` continues to the retry branch. Given a pins canon whose retry count has reached `cfg.approvals.auto_approve_after_retries`, on an L1 non-T3 site, with no person-only gate matched by `person_only_target(it, canon.verb, canon.target)`, `apply` returns a retry stamp and the agent gets an approval without a person. This also defeats the new tier-3 guard because that check is only inside `_rule_stamp`, while the retry path checks only `min_level <= 1`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The added documentation states that a `pins_regenerate` use “opens or extends the standing window, like any in-scope fire.” Because the standing window is the shared mechanism that suppresses human approval for verbs listed in `standing_verbs`, this documents a way for a non-gate command to widen coverage of other standing rules. For example, if the operator has enabled both `pins_regenerate` and `complete.force` in `approvals.policy`/`standing_verbs`, an agent can run `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` once for a live work item; per this text that opens/extends the standing window, and a later `ddflow complete --force` within `standing_window_s` can then be answered as `policy:complete.force` without a fresh person approval. That is wrong because `pins_regenerate` should not broaden the approval window available to other standing rules.

chunk_findings.detail:
`_work_item_of` returns the *first* line beginning with `"  work item: "`, and `used` uses that value to decide whether a recorded standing-rule use counts against the current work item. If the approval text contains any earlier line with that prefix—e.g. a reason, note, or drifted text—the function returns that earlier item and ignores the real trailing marker. Given a `pins_regenerate` policy answer for recipe `R` and item `T1` whose text is:
```text
  work item: T2
  work item: T1
  approved by standing rule: pins_regenerate
```
`used(state, "pins_regenerate", "R", "T1")` returns `0`, even though a use for `T1` was recorded. With `policy_max_uses=1`, a second regeneration of `R` for `T1` would pass the cap, violating the intended one-use-per-item limit. The previous anchored `endswith` check prevented this by matching only the recorded final marker.

chunk_findings.detail: `_recipe_untouched` only checks that `recipes_file` is clean in `repo` and that the recipe parsed from `repo` equals the recipe parsed from the current `primary`. It does not detect an edit that has been committed, nor an edit to `primary`. Given the common input where the agent runs the command in the same checkout (`repo == primary`) with `pins_regenerate` enabled, the agent can edit recipe `R`’s `regen` command in `recipes_file`, run `git add recipes_file && git commit`, then invoke `ddflow pins regenerate --only R` as an agent with no `--approval`. `git status --porcelain -- recipes_file` is empty, `mine == trusted` because both loads read the same committed edited file, so `_recipe_untouched` returns `True`; the edited-recipe guard is skipped and the standing rule answers, running the edited recipe without a person.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/pin_files.py:_recipe_untouched

chunk_findings.detail: The edited-recipe guard is bypassed when the agent supplies a non-empty approval value, including `--approval request`. The condition `not approval` is false for `CN.REQUEST`, so `_recipe_untouched` is never consulted even when the recipe has been edited. Given `pins_regenerate` enabled and recipe `R` edited, an agent can run `ddflow pins regenerate --only R --approval request`; the canonical approval is still `CN.REQUEST`, the request path that standing rules can answer, and the command can be answered without a person despite the edited recipe.

chunk_findings.detail: For a `PINS_VERB` canon, `apply` now resolves `it = _acting_item(state, canon, cfg)` before any enabled standing rule has been found. If `_rule_stamp` then returns `None` because `pins_regenerate` is absent from `cfg.approvals.policy`, because its window is closed, or because `policy_max_uses` has been exhausted, control falls through to the retry approval block. That block only checks `canon.site.min_level <= 1`, `retry_armed(cfg, canon)`, and `person_only_target(it, canon.verb, canon.target)`. Concrete input: `cfg.approvals.policy = []` (rule off), a recipe in the new default allowlist such as `readme-knobs` for which `_acting_item` finds a work item, an L1/non-T3 site, `auto_approve_after_retries` satisfied so `retry_armed(cfg, canon)` is true, and `person_only_target(...)` false. `apply` returns an approval for `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` even though the standing pins rule is off. Previously a pins canon named a recipe, so `state.items.get(canon.item)` was normally `None` and the function returned before the retry path; this change makes the retry path reachable for pins and bypasses the pins-specific enabled/window/use checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: `_rule_stamp` intentionally returns `None` when `canon.site.tier == sites.T3`, and its comment states that a policy answer is “never a tier-3 act.” However, the retry fallback in `apply` does not enforce tier. Given a tier-T3 site with `canon.site.min_level == 1`, `retry_armed(cfg, canon)` true, and `person_only_target(...)` false, `_rule_stamp` returns `None` at the tier check, then `apply` still enters the retry block and returns an approval. This lets a tier-3 act get an automatic answer without a person, violating the new invariant asserted in the same change.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/approvals/policy.py:apply

chunk_findings.detail: The new paragraph says “A use opens or extends the standing window, like any in-scope fire,” but the standing window is described earlier as a global window bounded by `standing_window_s` and `standing_verbs`, not as a per-rule window. With this documented behavior, an agent that gets one auto-approved `ddflow pins regenerate --only readme-knobs` can open or extend the same standing window that other enabled standing rules consume. For example, if `approvals.policy` includes both `pins_regenerate` and `complete.force`, and `standing_verbs` includes `pins.regenerate` and `complete.force`, the agent’s allowed regenerate fire can extend the global window and then a subsequent `complete.force` can be answered by policy without a person. That widens the scope of other standing rules beyond the explicit `pins_regenerate` approval and can defeat the expired-window bound by letting agent-triggered in-scope uses keep the window alive.
